newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Racal profits drop, aims for overhaul.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Racal profits drop, aims for overhaul.

text.p: Racal Electronics Plc vowed to do better for its shareholders on Tuesday after reporting a 42 percent fall in full-year headline profits.
The group said it was seeking partnerships for its British-based telecoms network business, as well as considering sell-offs in other parts of the group.

Pretax profits fell to 40.4 million pounds ($66 million) for the year to March 31 from 70.4 million pounds last time, after charging 29 million pounds for the cost of restructuring its Data Products division.

The company said profits were set to improve for the current full year, although margin pressures in its Telecommunications Services business and the costs of rationalisation would "adversely impact" the first-half result.
Racal plans to cut around a 1,000 jobs in Europe and the United States from its workforce of 15,000 this year, at a cost of 10 million pounds.
The share price rose 6-1/2 pence a share to 240 after the news, but had settled back to close at 235-1/2 pence, up 2p on the day in a slightly weaker overall market.
Racal has been under pressure to come up with a new strategy following a series of profit warnings and a 30 percent slump in its share price in the last year.
Recent press speculation had suggested that veteran chairman Sir Ernest Harrison would break up the group, or at least reshape it through a series of disposals, mergers and alliances.
Harrison sold Chubb Security to Williams Holdings for 1.1 billion pounds earlier this year after floating off mobile phones firm Vodafone in 1991.
Vodafone is now valued at over a billion pounds. In comparison, Racal is carrying a market value of around 660 million pounds.

Harrison said he was still looking at all options to improve shareholder value. He did not rule out keeping all three of the core telecoms, data communication products and defence electronics businesses and growing them in-house.

But he said mergers and acquisitions advisers were being recruited to explore the possibilities of joining up with another company to develop Racal's telecoms business, which had sales of 260 million pounds last year.
Options to be looked at included teaming up with overseas players creating global alliances, such as AT&T, or other European operators seeking to break out of their domestic markets.
Racal has already appointed investment bank Goldman Sachs to advise on strategy for its newly restructured U.S.-based electronic data products division.
"All options are open," Harrison said. "We will work on it but they have to be deals which are in the shareholders' interest and it may take some time."
"I am totally committed to...creating the greatest value for shareholders," Harrison told reporters.
"We have done that with Vodafone. We have done it with Chubb. Now I want to see Racal shareholders enjoy the real value inherent in our business."
Most immediately Racal hopes its troubled Data Products division is on track to move back into profit, following last year's radical restructuring.
Data Products made an operating loss during the restructuring of 19.1 million pounds on sales of 281 million pounds.
But the company said Data Products had since introduced a range of new products and these should start to bring in $70 million a year of additional "high margin" income.
"One thing which will dramatically change our profitability is Data Products," Harrison told a news conference.
"The most immediate key (to increasing shareholder value) is Data Products coming good." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717 ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
